title: Clonal selection of a B cell
caption: Each B cell carries a receptor for one antigen. The antigen selects the matching cell, a helper T cell activates it, and it multiplies into a clone. Most of the clone becomes plasma cells that secrete antibody; some become memory cells that make later responses faster.
alt: Four boxes in order: antigen meets its matching B cell, helper T cell activation, clonal expansion, and plasma cells and memory cells.
description: Antigen meets its B cell: only the B cell whose receptor matches binds it.
Helper T cell activation: the B cell presents the antigen; a helper T cell gives the signals.
Clonal expansion: the selected B cell divides again and again.
Plasma cells and memory cells: plasma cells secrete antibodies; memory B cells wait for a second exposure.
